_description: Standing macro/geopolitical situations referenced across briefings. Loader: scripts/generate_daily.py:load_ongoing_situations(). Manually maintained. Set status to 'resolved' when a situation is no longer relevant; the loader will skip it. Add new situations when they enter the briefing rotation. Keep facts list under 6 items per situation (loader caps at 6). Anchor phrase is the one-clause framing used on FIRST reference each week per Rule 18.

iran_hormuz.anchor: the Iran-Hormuz cycle — a July re-escalation (vessels hit, tankers reversing, crude running) that has since cooled, with the premium deflating again into August
facts: the situation re-escalated in early-to-mid July: commercial vessels hit, tanker traffic reversed course, and crude ran multi-percent sessions on Iran headlines
by late July the market's focus shifted from Hormuz risk to Red Sea/Houthi rerouting costs — two offsetting freight stories
as of Aug 3 the briefing's own read: crude supply building, Hormuz premium still deflating, no input-cost surprise
the premium has built and unwound twice since April — treat fresh escalation headlines as a known pattern, not a new regime
diesel tightness, not crude, has been the input-cost story for fall fieldwork

china_trade_deal.anchor: China's $17 billion annual US ag purchase commitment (May 18 deal, through 2028), now showing up as periodic confirmed soybean sales
facts: confirmed China soybean purchases have repeatedly lifted beans intraday in July, with a buy-the-rumor-sell-the-fact pattern capping follow-through
the commitment spans beans, beef, and poultry beyond prior soybean levels
beans set 52-week highs in late July with Chinese demand as one leg of the story (heat premium was the other)
US soybeans still face roughly 13% at the Chinese border (3% MFN + 10% retaliatory levy) — the truce holds through Nov 10, 2026
purchases have supported the board without producing a sustained trend on their own

cargill_fort_morgan_lockout.anchor: the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity
facts: 1,700 workers still locked out as of the end of July; no resolution announced
processing-constrained (not supply-constrained) price dynamics persist in fed cattle
any return-to-work agreement restores ~6,000 head daily and pressures feeders back toward $330
feedlot margins turned negative in late July, capping how far feeders can sustain above $340
watch item each week: lockout resolution reopens fed cattle price discovery

growing_season_2026.anchor: the 2026 growing season: a clean pollination window and rain-favored Belt that stripped the weather premium, with crop tour week (Aug 3+) now the arbiter
facts: corn's pollination window closed clean in late July; the briefing's read was 'crops healthier than the calendar usually allows'
Belt rain in the last week of July handed bears a clean exit — no weather bid until tour or heat says otherwise
Pro Farmer crop tour scouts are in fields the week of Aug 3; their numbers are the next real catalyst before the Aug 12 WASDE
AGSIST's own nowcast (ratings-based): corn 184.1, beans 53.8 vs USDA trend 183.0/53.0 — above trend, wide early-August bands
December corn carries the story now; old-crop/new-crop corn carry was $0.23 into the roll

cattle_mexico_screwworm.anchor: the screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports, with the first phased port reopening set for Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ
facts: the border closure has quietly tightened feeder supply all summer and is one leg of the historic feeder rally
USDA confirmed a phased reopening starting Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ — the dated supply headwind feeders are now pricing
feeders broke ~3% in late July as the market began pricing returning supply rather than yesterday's scarcity
the feeder/live spread is the tell: watch it as the Aug 24 date approaches
screwworm spread beyond Texas earlier in the season; containment progress drives the reopening pace

farm_bill_2026.anchor: the 2026 Farm Bill endgame: revised Senate text (Aug 1) with year-round E15 now in the bill, committee markup Aug 6, against the Sep 30 extension deadline
facts: the House passed H.R. 7567 in April; the Senate's Aug 1 revised text added year-round E15 sales — a real structural corn-demand tailwind once enacted
Senate Ag Committee markup is scheduled Thursday Aug 6, the day before the Senate recess; floor passage needs 60 votes
the Aug 1 text delays the SNAP state cost-share a year (FY2029; FY2031 for high-error states) — aimed at Democratic holdouts
a separate $15-17B economic-aid push (June White House request: $11B+) sits outside the bill; no program details exist yet
the current extension expires Sep 30, 2026 — the hard date for a bill or another extension
